main_text.p: proponeret nomé,tota mea fubstatia, omnefq; ꝓprietates perfectissime declaras,nü eo nomineappellatus ab illo, cogerer eius imperio obsequi, & quæ-cūq; ille vellet facere? Si recoditissima illa vim & efficaciam vocū Hebræarū quā iactat Cabalistæ, paucissimi homi-nū intelligūt,nec nisi qui illa eadé ante sunt initiati, quomodo eā agnoscet & sentiet bruta, ceteraq; nō ratione solū, sed etiā sensu caretia? Cur tribuūt tātā vim vocibus & characteribus Hebreæ linguæ, quam omnium vetustissimam & primā ferunt, cum certe cōstet alios esse characteres Hebrēos,qui nunc exstāt, quam qui olim fuerāt ante captiuitatē Babyloniḉa? Quod beatus Hieronymus in Prologo galeato affirmate scribit.Certū,inquit,est,Esdra post captam Hierosolyma,& restauratione tēpli sub Zorobabele,alias literas reperisse,quibus nunc vtimur,cū ad illud vsq; tēpus side Samaritanorū & Hebræorum characteres fuerint. Nec verum est, in lingua Hebræa reperiri voces,quæ omnium rerum naturas, infimasq; differetias &proprietates expri-mat, nec in declarandis rebus vberiore

page.notes: Right-hand edge of the page is damaged by the scan. Some letters in the lower lines are uncertain; the text is transcribed as far as legible. Verse of the title "Pars Altera" is printed as a running head.
